key_insight: In multimodal diffusion transformers, image-to-text feedback does not just correct the prompt—it can also lock in whatever the image has already started to represent, including mistakes. By suppressing this feedback, the paper shows how model behavior can change, and even how messages from one generation can be transplanted to rescue failures or break good outputs.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the question of whether image-to-text feedback in MMDiTs helps steer generations back toward the prompt or instead preserves early image states, including incorrect objects and attributes.
method: Analyze the role of image-to-text (I2T) feedback inside joint-attention multimodal diffusion transformers.
Suppress I2T feedback to test how much it influences image fidelity, error persistence, and prompt alignment.
Transplant I2T messages between generations to probe whether feedback can rescue failures or disrupt otherwise successful outputs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work clarifies a hidden control mechanism in multimodal generation models. It suggests a new way to improve or debug MMDiTs by managing feedback paths rather than only tuning prompts or sampling.

paper_title: Images Talk Back: Guiding MMDiTs by Suppressing Image-to-Text Feedback
paper_authors: Yucheng Yang, Xiaoxiao Sun, Shusheng Yang, Jiakang Chen, Serena Yeung-Levy
